Definition: feminine of G2272; (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language:--quietness, silence.
BiblicalUsage: I take hēsychía to mean quietness, silence, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 4 times, and Acts and 2 Thessalonians show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: hēsychía matters to me because stillness is not laziness — it is trust that God is at work. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
